lane: Phase 2 backend: step 2b, register the Singapore staging target and its own migration ledger for Owner review
goal: Prepare, for a separate Owner-reviewed pull request, the release-profile allowlist entry for the Singapore staging target, a target-specific migration ledger and a draft database-target manifest bound to the approved SQL set, without running SQL, changing the legacy ledger or retargeting any runtime.
successCriteria: docs/release/release-profile.json lists exactly one target: nilaza-singapore-prelaunch-qa, kind staging, organization drxbmvimiekeoeesgssp, project etfajmrwyywokgafzxsb, matching the existing staging resource policy; no production target is added.

A new ledger for the Singapore target records the empty migration history read on 2026-10-26 and does not touch supabase/migration-ledger.json, which stays blocked_pending_reconciliation for the legacy QA project.

A draft database-target manifest binds the target, profile hash, ledger hash and the 31 approved migrations; scripts/database-target-gate.mjs reports BLOCKED (not FAIL) and lists the evidence still missing for step 2c.
The approval form explains decision 2b with object, risk and rollback, and explains that the gate's migration-set hash is a different encoding of the same 31 files approved in 2a.
The release-control skill reference no longer says the allowlist is empty, and its manifest hash is updated through the reviewed path.
Existing gate, release-evidence, preflight and ledger checks still pass; no secret appears in any changed file.
untouchedSurfaces: supabase/migration-ledger.json (legacy QA akgrokwnkfqnfjqrildi) stays blocked_pending_reconciliation and is not relabeled.
Migration files, seed, packet-manifest.json and replay-receipt.json are unchanged, so the 2a approval hashes stay valid.
No production target is registered; production promotion remains a separate decision.
Mobile, Admin, EAS and Vercel runtime bindings still point at the legacy QA project; no retarget.
No SQL, migration, Edge Function deployment, secret or cloud setting is executed, read or changed.

impact.entryPoint: Owner approved decision 2a on 2026-10-26 and asked on 2026-10-27 for step 2b to be prepared locally without pushing.
impact.dataWrite: Repository files only: release profile allowlist entry, a new target ledger, a draft target manifest and documentation.
impact.backendContract: No API, schema or contract change; the release checker will now see one registered staging target.
impact.adminVisibility: No Admin change. Merging to main later triggers an Admin staging deployment with unchanged behavior.
impact.privacySafety: Files contain public project identifiers, counts and hashes only; the target has 0 Auth users.
impact.observability: The draft manifest and gate output list exactly what evidence step 2c still needs.
impact.rollback: Revert the 2b commit or pull request; the allowlist returns to empty and the new ledger and draft manifest disappear. No cloud state depends on them.

canonicalContracts: AGENTS.md: the Owner approves cloud SQL, retargeting and release actions; the target allowlist stays empty until reviewed mapping is approved.
docs/PLAN_QC_PROTOCOL.md: plan, impact map, validation and handoff quality gate.
scripts/database-target-gate.mjs: target manifest, ledger, metadata, replay and approval evidence contract.
docs/production/2026-10-04/database-target-gate.vi.md: do not relabel the legacy ledger; a new project needs its own ledger.

sourceReview.reason: Owner boundaries and the allowlist rule reviewed.
Routing reviewed; release and backend gates are the routed area.
Evidence contract for target, ledger, migrations, metadata, replay and approval; its migration-set hash is JSON-encoded, unlike the packet manifest.
Confirmed it validates only the legacy ledger path, which stays unchanged.
Legacy QA ledger reviewed and intentionally left blocked.
Target-gate guide followed for the ledger and manifest shape.
Allowlist entry added to match the existing staging resource policy.
Reviewed hash for the updated release-control reference.

skillReview.name: nilaza-plan-qc
skillReview.evidence: references/release-control.md said the cloud target allowlist is intentionally empty; it now says one staging target is proposed, that the legacy ledger is not relabeled and that registration does not authorize SQL.

dependencyReview.evidence: No external documentation or service behavior is relied on; target state comes from the first-party read-only readback of 2026-10-26 recorded in readback-2026-10-26.json.

securityReview.authzRls: No authorization or RLS change; the allowlist entry is staging only and the gate still blocks without fresh metadata, replay with restore and RLS acceptance, and an exact owner approval.
securityReview.sensitiveData: No user data; the target has 0 Auth users.
securityReview.secretsLogging: No key, password or token is read, recorded or requested.
securityReview.externalInput: Readback values are treated as data.
securityReview.migrationRelease: No migration, SQL write, retarget, signing or store submission; registration does not authorize execution.
securityReview.stopCondition: Stop if the gate reports FAIL for the draft manifest, if any approved packet hash changes, or if the legacy ledger would need to change.

validationCommands: Search the changed files for secret-like patterns
managerTestPath: Open the 2b section of 05_STEP2_APPROVAL_FORM.vi.md and check that it names one staging target, shows what changes and what does not, and says how to undo it.
residualRisk: Registering the target makes the release checkers treat Singapore staging as an allowed target; execution still needs fresh evidence and decision 2c. The ledger readback ages out after 24 hours by design and must be refreshed right before 2c.
